# Picasso Intelligence

> Authorized CubeMars distributor for North America. Robotic actuators, frameless and gimbal motors and underwater thrusters, sold and supported from the United States.

Prices are in US dollars and are what the site charges. Import duty on orders to the United States is paid by us, so there is no carrier invoice after delivery. Shipping within the United States is free on orders over $200 and $45 below that. Orders above $5,000 and all orders outside the United States are quoted individually.

## AK Series

- [AK40-10 KV170](https://picassointelligence.com/ak40-10-kv170-without-driver.html): US$112. The smallest joint in the AK line: brushless motor, planetary reducer, encoder and driver in one housing. Sized for the places an actuator has to disappear into the limb — humanoid wrists, grippers, small pan-tilt heads. Supplied without the driver board.
- [AK45-10 KV75](https://picassointelligence.com/ak45-10-kv75-without-driver.html): US$134. A wider, slower AK40-10: the same 53 mm frame and 10:1 reduction, wound for roughly twice the torque at half the speed. The usual pick when a wrist or elbow needs holding torque more than it needs travel. Supplied without the driver board.
- [AK40-10 V3.0 KV170](https://picassointelligence.com/ak40-10-v3-0-kv170.html): US$152. 1.3 N·m rated and 4.1 N·m peak from a Ф53 x 40.2 mm, 190 g frame, geared 10:1, on 24 V. Kv 170, 370 RPM rated and 435 RPM no-load. CubeMars lists it for legged robots, exoskeletons and AGVs.
- [AK45-36 KV80](https://picassointelligence.com/ak45-36-kv80-without-driver.html): US$168. A 36:1 reduction in the 55 mm frame, which is what turns a small actuator into a load-holding one — the torque of a joint half again its diameter, at a speed to match. That trade suits a joint that spends most of its time holding a position rather than moving through one: an ankle, a wrist, a...
- [AK45-10 V3.0 KV75](https://picassointelligence.com/ak45-10-v3-0-kv75.html): US$175. 2.5 N·m rated and 7 N·m peak from a Ф53 x 45.2 mm, 262 g frame, geared 10:1, on 24 V. Kv 75, 120 RPM rated and 180 RPM no-load. CubeMars lists it for legged robots, exoskeletons and AGVs.
- [AK45-36 V3.0 KV80](https://picassointelligence.com/ak45-36-v3-0-kv80.html): US$208. The V3.0 revision of the AK45-36: the same 36:1 gearing and torque density, on the current driver board and the V3.0 configuration tool. Dual encoders, on the rotor and the output, so the joint reports where the load actually is rather than where the motor thinks it put it.
- [AK60-6 V3.0 KV80](https://picassointelligence.com/ak60-6-v3-0-kv80.html): US$335. 3 N·m rated and 9 N·m peak from a Ф79 x 43 mm, 380 g frame, geared 6:1, on 24 V. Kv 80, 233 RPM rated. CubeMars lists it for legged robots, exoskeletons and AGVs.
- [AK60-6 V1.1 KV140](https://picassointelligence.com/ak60-6-v1-1-kv140.html): US$335. 3 N·m rated and 9 N·m peak from a Ф79 x 39.5 mm, 368 g frame, geared 6:1, on 24 V. Kv 140, 420 RPM rated. CubeMars lists it for legged robots, exoskeletons and AGVs.
- [AK70-9 V3.0 KV60 without driver](https://picassointelligence.com/ak70-9-v3-0-kv60-without-driver.html): US$447. The mid-size V3.0 joint, at the ratio where a planetary reducer stops costing much speed — 9:1 on an 89 mm frame. Legs, shoulders, and anything that has to move as well as hold. Supplied without the driver board.
- [AK70-10 KV100 without driver](https://picassointelligence.com/ak70-10-kv100-without-driver.html): US$447. 8.3 N·m rated and 24.8 N·m peak from a Ф89 x 50.25 mm, 621 g frame, geared 10:1, on 24 V. Kv 100, 148 RPM rated. CubeMars lists it for legged robots, exoskeletons and AGVs.
- [AK60-39 V3.0](https://picassointelligence.com/ak60-39-v3-0.html): US$503. Two planetary stages for a 39:1 reduction, so a 79 mm joint holds what an unreduced one its size could not. Dual magnetic encoders on both sides of the gearbox, and speed, torque, position and MIT modes.
- [AK80-8 KV60 without driver](https://picassointelligence.com/ak80-8-kv60-without-driver.html): US$526. 10 N·m rated and 25 N·m peak from a Ф98 x 43.9 mm, 570 g frame, geared 8:1, on 48 V. Kv 60, 243 RPM rated. CubeMars lists it for legged robots, exoskeletons and AGVs.
- [AK80-9 V3.0 KV100 without driver](https://picassointelligence.com/ak80-9-v3-0-kv100-without-driver.html): US$537. 9 N·m rated and 22 N·m peak from a Ф98 x 38.5 mm, 490 g frame, geared 9:1, on 48 V. Kv 100, 390 RPM rated and 570 RPM no-load. CubeMars lists it for legged robots, exoskeletons and AGVs.

- [AK70-9 V3.0 KV60 with driver](https://picassointelligence.com/ak70-9-v3-0-kv60-with-driver.html): US$559. The mid-size V3.0 joint, at the ratio where a planetary reducer stops costing much speed — 9:1 on an 89 mm frame. Legs, shoulders, and anything that has to move as well as hold. ## AKA Series

- [AKA60-6 KV80](https://picassointelligence.com/aka60-6-kv80.html): US$335. The AKA series is suitable for applications with high radial loads such as wheeled robots and AGVs. This series of products adopts a completely new structural design scheme.
- [AKA10-9 KV60](https://picassointelligence.com/aka10-9-kv60.html): US$895. The AKA series is suitable for applications with high radial loads, such as wheeled robots and AGVs.

## AKE Series

- [AKE40-6 KV90](https://picassointelligence.com/ake40-6-kv90.html): US$134. The smallest AKE: 140 g and 24.5 mm deep, for 1.8 N·m continuous and 5.5 N·m peak at 9 arcmin of backlash. The weight is the point — on a limb, every gram at the far end is carried by every joint above it.
- [AKE50-8 KV110](https://picassointelligence.com/ake50-8-kv110.html): US$190. 190 g and 22.5 mm deep for 2.5 N·m continuous and 7.5 N·m peak, at the same 9 arcmin of backlash as the rest of the series. The flattest joint CubeMars make at this torque.
- [AKE60-8 KV80](https://picassointelligence.com/ake60-8-kv80.html): US$245. 5 N·m rated and 12.5 N·m peak from a Ф69 x 25 mm, 260 g frame, geared 8:1, on 24 V. Kv 80, 180 RPM rated and 240 RPM no-load. CubeMars lists it for exoskeletons.
- [AKE80-8 KV30](https://picassointelligence.com/ake80-8-kv30.html): US$381. 12 N·m rated and 30 N·m peak from a Ф87 x 32 mm, 570 g frame, geared 8:1, on 48 V. Kv 30, 150 RPM rated and 195 RPM no-load. CubeMars lists it for exoskeletons.
- [AKE90-8 KV35](https://picassointelligence.com/ake90-8-kv35.html): US$542. CubeMars' AKE90-8 KV35 Quasi Direct Drive is the ideal choice for the industrial automation and robotics.

## AKH Series

- [AKH70-16 V1.0 KV41](https://picassointelligence.com/akh70-16-v1-0-kv41.html): US$670. A two-stage 16:1 hollow-shaft joint. Power and signal run through the middle of the output rather than around the outside of it, which is what lets an arm keep rotating without a service loop.
- [AKH70-48 V1.0 KV41](https://picassointelligence.com/akh70-48-v1-0-kv41.html): US$782. Three planetary stages for 48:1, through a hollow output shaft. Dual encoders on both sides of the gearbox, so the controller sees the load and not just the motor.

## Direct Drive Motors

- [MyActuator RMD-L-4010](https://picassointelligence.com/rmd-l-4010.html): US$140. A 40 mm direct drive with the driver built in: 0.15 N·m continuous off the rotor with no gearbox between it and the output, so there is no backlash to take up and nothing to wear. 92 g, CAN bus, 24 V.
- [MyActuator RMD-H-50-15](https://picassointelligence.com/rmd-h-50-15.html): US$180. A 50 mm direct drive with a 16 mm hollow bore through the middle, so the harness runs through the joint instead of around it. 0.35 N·m continuous, 0.9 N·m peak, no gearbox and no backlash.

## Choosing a part

- [Actuators for Humanoid Robots](https://picassointelligence.com/actuators-for-humanoid-robots.html): Joint modules from wrist to hip. Distal joints are chosen on weight, proximal joints on torque.
- [Actuators for Exoskeletons](https://picassointelligence.com/actuators-for-exoskeletons.html): Backdrivable joints at low reduction, where the wearer has to be able to push the actuator around.
- [Actuators for Quadruped Robots](https://picassointelligence.com/actuators-for-quadruped-robots.html): High peak torque with enough transparency to run a torque loop on the leg.
- [Actuators for Cobot and Medical Arms](https://picassointelligence.com/actuators-for-cobot-and-medical-arms.html): Low backlash and hollow output shafts, so power and CAN run inside the arm instead of around it.
- [Actuators for Wheeled Robots and AGVs](https://picassointelligence.com/actuators-for-wheeled-robots-and-agvs.html): Built for the radial load a driven wheel puts on the output bearing.
- [Actuators for Gimbals and Sensor Pods](https://picassointelligence.com/actuators-for-gimbals-and-sensor-pods.html): Direct drive with low cogging, so the pod holds its aim at near-zero speed.
- [How to read a CubeMars part number](https://picassointelligence.com/part-numbers.html): what the digits mean in AK, AKE, AKH, RI, RO, GL, SW, DW and TW names, and which of them CubeMars does not publish.
- [Find by specification](https://picassointelligence.com/select.html): every part on one table, sortable by torque, diameter, weight or price.
